name: Farm Operating Loans (Direct and Guaranteed)
description: FSA Farm Operating Loans help farmers and ranchers pay for livestock, equipment, feed, seed and supplies, minor improvements, family living expenses and the refinancing of certain debts. Direct loans come from FSA itself. Guaranteed loans are made by commercial lenders, and FSA guarantees them.
eligibleEntities: U.S. citizens, non-citizen nationals, or qualified aliens
eligibleActivities: Purchase of livestock, poultry and farm equipment
Feed, seed, fuel, farm chemicals, insurance and other operating expenses
Family living expenses
Minor improvements or repairs to buildings and fencing
Refinancing certain debts (under specific conditions)
financialCriteria: Satisfactory credit history
Ability to repay the loan
Inability to obtain credit elsewhere at reasonable rates and terms (direct loans)
For guaranteed loans: be unable to obtain a loan without an FSA guarantee
Not delinquent on any Federal debt (guaranteed loans)
agriculturalCriteria: Operate a family farm (case-by-case review: family makes day-to-day management decisions and provides significant labor)
Be the operator of a family farm after the loan is closed (guaranteed operating loans)
fundingRange: Direct Operating Loans: Provided directly by the FSA, up to $400,000. Guaranteed Operating Loans: Issued by commercial lenders but guaranteed by the FSA, up to $2,558,000 (amount adjusted annually based on inflation).
deadline: No fixed deadline stated; enrollment instructions and deadlines are available through the local FSA office.
requiredDocuments: Loan application submitted to local FSA office
Detailed financial and production information
Comprehensive farm business plan
For guaranteed loans: Application for Guarantee completed by the lender and the applicant
verificationNotes: Checked the eligibility, loan purposes and loan limits on the FSA operating loans page, plus the guaranteed-loan rules on https://www.fsa.usda.gov/resources/loans/guaranteed-farm-loans. Current interest rates are on a separate page and were not recorded.
fitRationale: Direct loans require that the borrower cannot get credit elsewhere, and guaranteed loans require that a lender would not lend without FSA's guarantee. A profitable $3.8M-revenue operation buying $250K of equipment can probably get conventional credit. A lender could still ask for a guarantee in some cases.

name: Farm Ownership Loans (Direct and Guaranteed)
description: FSA Farm Ownership Loans help farmers and ranchers buy, develop or expand an operation, including buying farmland, building farm buildings and improving existing structures. The loans come as direct FSA loans, commercial loans guaranteed by FSA, a Down Payment Program for beginning farmers, or joint financing with other lenders.
eligibleActivities: Farmland purchase
Construction or repair of farm buildings and other fixtures
Improvements to existing structures and infrastructure
Developing farmland to promote soil and water conservation (guaranteed)
Refinancing debt (guaranteed)
financialCriteria: Demonstrate an ability to repay the loan
For guaranteed loans: be unable to obtain a loan without an FSA guarantee
For guaranteed loans: acceptable credit history as determined by the lender
Not delinquent on any Federal debt (guaranteed loans)
agriculturalCriteria: Sufficient education, training, or experience in managing a farm
For guaranteed Farm Ownership loans: be the owner-operator of a family farm after the loan is closed
fundingRange: Direct Loans: Up to $600,000. Guaranteed Loans: Up to $2,558,000. Down Payment Program: Up to 45% of the purchase price or appraised value.
deadline: No fixed deadline stated; enrollment instructions and deadlines are available through the local FSA office.
requiredDocuments: Loan application submitted to local FSA office
Documentation of financial history
Farm business plan
For guaranteed loans: Application for Guarantee completed by the lender and the applicant
verificationNotes: Checked the loan types, loan amounts, repayment terms of up to 40 years and the general eligibility on the FSA ownership loans page. The 'unable to obtain a loan without a guarantee' rule comes from FSA's guaranteed-loans page. That page does not say whether direct ownership loans have the same credit-elsewhere test.
fitRationale: A possible $1M land purchase fits within the guaranteed limit. Whether a guarantee applies depends on the farm's existing debt and leverage, and on whether its lender would make the loan without one, and we do not have that information. The Down Payment Program is aimed at beginning farmers, which this 20+ year operation is not.

name: Environmental Quality Incentives Program (EQIP)
description: EQIP gives agricultural producers technical and financial help to put conservation practices in place. The practices address resource concerns such as soil, water and air quality, nutrient and pest management, and energy conservation. Participants carry out an NRCS-approved EQIP plan of operations under a contract.
geography: Nationwide (US), including DC and US territories
eligibleEntities: Legal entities (must list all members and their percentage interest)
eligibleActivities: NRCS-approved conservation practices (list published by NRCS)
Soil and water quality practices
Nutrient management
Pest management
Energy conservation
Wildlife habitat practices
financialCriteria: Payment eligibility under 7 CFR part 1400, including adjusted gross income provisions
Subject to EQIP contract and aggregate payment limitations
agriculturalCriteria: Comply with highly erodible land and wetland conservation provisions (7 CFR part 12)
Have control of the land for the term of the contract (tenants may need written landowner concurrence)
Develop and implement an EQIP plan of operations
Practices started before application or contract approval are generally ineligible for payment
fundingRange: Each contract will be limited to no more than $450,000, unless the contract is with an Indian Tribe or the Chief grants a waiver.
deadline: Applications may be accepted on a continuous basis throughout the year; ranking periods are set by NRCS.
requiredDocuments: EQIP application
EQIP plan of operations
List of all legal entity members with tax identification numbers and percentage interest
Information to determine payment eligibility (7 CFR part 1400)
verificationNotes: The NRCS program page (nrcs.usda.gov) timed out repeatedly, so every fact here comes from the official regulation, 7 CFR part 1466 on eCFR. The regulation's aggregate limit ($450,000) is worded for FY2019-2023, and we could not confirm the current aggregate limit, the Iowa ranking dates or the payment rates.
fitRationale: An Iowa row-crop operation interested in cover crops and conservation fits EQIP's purpose. Funding is competitive and ranked by NRCS. The ~1,600 cash-rented acres need control of the land for the contract term and possibly the landowner's written concurrence.

name: Conservation Stewardship Program (CSP)
description: CSP pays producers who already meet conservation stewardship thresholds to improve, maintain and manage existing conservation activities and to add new ones across their whole operation. Payments are annual. Supplemental payments are available for resource-conserving crop rotations, and cover crop activities are paid at an enhanced rate.
geography: Nationwide (US), including DC and US territories
eligibleEntities: Operators, owners, or tenants of an agricultural operation in FSA farm records
Legal entities and joint operations (must list all members, tax IDs and percentage interest)
eligibleActivities: Additional conservation activities (enhancements)
Improving, maintaining and managing existing conservation activities
Cover crop activities (paid at not less than 125% of the annual payment amount)
Resource-conserving crop rotations (supplemental payment)
Comprehensive conservation plan (one-time payment)
financialCriteria: Compliance with adjusted gross income provisions (7 CFR part 1400)
Must provide a tax identification number
agriculturalCriteria: Share in the risk of producing a crop and participate in daily management of the operation
Have effective control of the land
Comply with highly erodible land and wetland conservation provisions (7 CFR part 12)
Meet or exceed the stewardship threshold for at least two priority resource concerns at application, and at least one more by the end of the contract
Application must include all eligible land in the agricultural operation
fundingRange: Each conservation stewardship contract will be limited to $200,000 over the term of the contract period, except that conservation stewardship contracts with any joint operation will be limited to $400,000 over the term of the contract period.
deadline: Applicants may submit an application for CSP at any time; applications are ranked in periods set by NRCS.
requiredDocuments: CSP application covering all eligible land
Current FSA farm records for the operator and land
List of legal entity members with tax identification numbers and percentage interest
Information on conservation activity and production system records
verificationNotes: The NRCS program page (nrcs.usda.gov) timed out repeatedly, so these facts come from the official regulation, 7 CFR part 1470 on eCFR. The regulation's $200,000 aggregate cap per person or entity is worded for FY2019-2023, and we could not confirm current caps or Iowa ranking dates.
fitRationale: CSP rewards conservation an operation already practices plus new activities such as cover crops. Whether Smith Family Farms meets the two-resource-concern stewardship threshold, with all of its owned and rented land included, needs an NRCS assessment.

name: Rural Energy for America Program (REAP) Renewable Energy Systems & Energy Efficiency Improvement Guaranteed Loans & Grants
description: REAP provides grants and loan guarantees to agricultural producers and rural small businesses for renewable energy systems (RES) and for energy efficiency improvements (EEI). An improvement must use less energy each year than the equipment it replaces. Grants cover part of eligible project costs and can be combined with a guaranteed loan.
geography: Nationwide (US); agricultural producers may be in rural or non-rural areas
eligibleEntities: Agricultural producers (50% or more of gross income from agricultural operations)
eligibleActivities: Purchase of a new or refurbished renewable energy system
Retrofitting an existing renewable energy system
Energy efficiency improvements to buildings or equipment that reduce annual energy use
Combined grant and guaranteed loan financing
financialCriteria: Satisfactory sources of revenue to operate, maintain and service any debt on the project for its useful life
Grant limited to 25% of eligible project costs (unless a Federal Register notice says otherwise)
Combined grant and guaranteed loan may not exceed 75% of eligible project costs; applicant provides the remainder
Active SAM registration and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI)
agriculturalCriteria: 50 percent or greater of gross income derived from agricultural operations (averaged over the five most recent years)
Must own the project and own or control the project site
Project must use commercially available technology and have technical merit
EEI savings must be shown by vendor/installer certification or an energy assessment/audit
fundingRange: Unless otherwise specified in a Federal Register notice, the minimum request for a RES grant application is $2,500 and the minimum request for an EEI grant application is $1,500. ... the maximum request for a RES grant application is $500,000 and the maximum request for an EEI grant application is $250,000.
deadline: Per regulation (unless changed by Federal Register notice): complete applications due to the State Office by 4:30 p.m. local time March 31 for the State and National competitions; requests of $20,000 or less also compete in an October 31 state round.
requiredDocuments: SF-424 Application for Federal Assistance
SF-424C Budget Information for Construction Programs
SF-424D Assurances for Construction Programs
Form RD 4280-3A (projects $80,000 or less) or the full application for larger projects
Energy assessment or energy audit (EEI projects, as applicable)
Environmental documentation (7 CFR part 1970)
Applicant eligibility certifications
verificationNotes: rd.usda.gov returned 403 Access Denied, so these facts come from the official regulation, 7 CFR 4280 subpart B on eCFR. Federal Register notices can override the cost-share percentages, maximum amounts and deadlines, and we could not check the current notice or Iowa state-office dates.
fitRationale: A grain farm that gets nearly all of its income from farming meets the agricultural-producer definition, and a more efficient grain dryer or an on-farm renewable system such as solar would plausibly count as an energy efficiency improvement or renewable energy system project (the regulation does not name specific equipment). Awards are competitive, and the farm would need an energy assessment or audit and SAM registration.

name: Farm Storage Facility Loan (FSFL) Program
agency: USDA Farm Service Agency (on behalf of the Commodity Credit Corporation)
description: FSFL provides low-interest financing for producers to build or upgrade permanent and portable storage facilities and equipment for eligible commodities, including grains and oilseeds. Eligible items include grain bins, drying and handling equipment, and storage and handling trucks, new or used.
eligibleEntities: Producers of eligible commodities (grains, oilseeds, and others listed by FSA)
eligibleActivities: Building or upgrading grain bins and other storage facilities
Drying and handling equipment
Storage and handling trucks
New or used, permanently affixed or portable facilities and equipment
financialCriteria: 15 percent down payment for a regular FSFL (5 percent for microloans up to $50,000)
Regular three-year production history requirement (waived for microloans)
agriculturalCriteria: Produce an eligible commodity (corn and soybeans fall under grains/oilseeds)
fundingRange: The maximum loan amount for storage facilities is $500,000. The maximum loan amount for storage and handling trucks is $100,000.
deadline: No application deadline stated on the program page.
requiredDocuments: Form CCC-0185 (FSFL application)
verificationNotes: Checked the eligible commodities and equipment (including drying and handling), the loan maximums, the 3-12 year terms, the down payments and the October 2026 CCC rates (4.500%-5.000%) on the FSFL page. The page does not list detailed eligibility criteria such as credit or crop insurance requirements.
fitRationale: A 2,400-acre corn and soybean operation with a long production history fits the commodity and history rules, and grain drying and handling equipment is explicitly eligible. Fit depends on whether the planned $250K equipment purchase includes storage or drying rather than field machinery, which FSFL does not cover.

name: Emergency Conservation Program (ECP)
description: ECP provides financial and technical help to rehabilitate farmland damaged by natural disasters such as floods, wildfires, drought and other calamities. It pays a share of the cost of approved restoration practices such as debris removal, land re-leveling, fence restoration and emergency water conservation measures.
geography: Nationwide (US); available in areas with announced signups after a qualifying disaster
eligibleEntities: Farmers and ranchers whose farmland was damaged by a natural disaster
eligibleActivities: Removing post-disaster debris from farmland
Grading, shaping, or re-leveling land
Restoring permanent fences
Restoring water conservation structures
Emergency water conservation measures during severe drought
financialCriteria: Funding subject to congressional appropriations, first-come, first-served
agriculturalCriteria: Damage must significantly impair the land's agricultural productivity or threaten land or water resources
Damage must be so costly that federal assistance is required to return land to productive agricultural use
fundingRange: ECP provides cost-share assistance of up to 75% of the allowable cost of approved conservation practices. Limited resource producers may be eligible for up to 90% cost-share.
deadline: Applications are accepted during announced signup periods following a natural disaster event.
requiredDocuments: Request for assistance submitted to local FSA office
Documentation of the disaster impact / damage assessment
Description of the proposed restoration measures
verificationNotes: Checked the eligibility, covered practices, cost-share rates and signup approach on the FSA ECP page. We did not check whether any ECP signup is currently open in Story County, Iowa.
fitRationale: ECP applies only when a natural disaster has damaged farmland and FSA has announced a local signup. The profile does not mention any recent disaster damage, so this depends on events. (The ad-hoc Supplemental Disaster Relief Program for 2023/2024 losses closed on Sep. 30, 2026.)

name: Agriculture Risk Coverage (ARC) & Price Loss Coverage (PLC)
description: ARC and PLC pay producers when revenue for a covered commodity falls below a guarantee (ARC) or when the effective price falls below its effective reference price (PLC). Producers choose ARC-County or PLC crop by crop, or ARC-Individual for the whole farm, and must enroll through a signed contract each year.
eligibleEntities: Agricultural producers with an interest in a covered commodity grown on a farm with base acres
Landowners only if they have a share interest in the crops on the farm
eligibleActivities: Income/price support payments for covered commodities including corn and soybeans
financialCriteria: Producer must enroll through a signed contract each year (multi-year contract option for 2026-2031)
agriculturalCriteria: Farm must have base acres
Interest in a covered commodity (22 covered commodities including corn and soybeans)
Landowners need a share interest in the crops on the farm to enroll
deadline: 2026 Election and Enrollment - Sept. 16 through Dec. 11, 2026; 2027 Election and Enrollment - Nov. 2, 2026, through March 15, 2027
requiredDocuments: Signed ARC/PLC election and enrollment contract (through local FSA office)
Appendix to ARC/PLC Contracts (CCC-862-866 Appendix)
verificationNotes: Checked the eligibility, the covered commodities (corn and soybeans included), the 2026 and 2027 enrollment dates and the new base acre allocation (30M acres, prorated down 3.69%) on the FSA ARC/PLC page. The page does not state payment rates or payment limits, so the funding range is null.
fitRationale: Corn and soybeans are covered commodities, and the 2026 enrollment window is open now (through Dec. 11, 2026). Fit depends on the farmed acres carrying base acres and on Smith Family Farms having a share interest in the crops, which a cash-rent operator normally has.

name: Value-Added Producer Grants (VAPG)
description: VAPG funds agricultural producers' for-profit businesses that produce and market value-added agricultural products. Planning grants pay for feasibility studies, business plans and marketing plans. Working capital grants pay operating expenses for processing and marketing a value-added product.
eligibleActivities: Planning grants: feasibility study, business plan and/or marketing plan for a value-added product
Working capital grants: expenses for processing and/or marketing a value-added agricultural product
financialCriteria: Matching funds at least equal to the grant amount (grant covers up to 50% of project costs)
Active SAM registration and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI)
agriculturalCriteria: Must produce and own more than 50 percent of the agricultural commodity to which value will be added
Must maintain ownership of the commodity from raw state through production and marketing of the value-added product
Must be currently producing the agricultural commodity for each value-added product
fundingRange: Grant funds may be used to pay up to 50 percent of the Project Costs ... in no event may the total amount of grant funds provided to a grant Recipient exceed $500,000. (Annual maximum is set in the annual program notification.)
deadline: Application period and annual maximum grant amounts are announced in an annual notification on the program website.
requiredDocuments: SF-424 Application for Federal Assistance
SF-424A Budget Information - Non-Construction Programs
One-page executive summary
Eligibility discussion
Documentation of matching funds
Any additional forms listed in the annual notification
verificationNotes: rd.usda.gov returned 403 Access Denied, so these facts come from the official regulation, 7 CFR 4284 subpart J on eCFR. We could not confirm the current fiscal year's application window or per-grant maximums from the annual notice.
fitRationale: Smith Family Farms grows and sells commodity corn and soybeans. Nothing in the profile suggests processing or marketing a value-added product, which VAPG requires. It would fit only if the family launched a value-added venture.

name: Beginning Farmer Loan Program (BFLP)
agency: Iowa Agricultural Development Division (IADD), Iowa Finance Authority
description: The Iowa Beginning Farmer Loan Program helps new farmers buy agricultural property with loans at reduced interest rates, typically 20 to 25 percent below prevailing market rates. Loans can fund agricultural land, depreciable machinery or equipment, breeding livestock or buildings. They cannot be used to refinance existing debt.
eligibleEntities: Iowa residents age 18 or older (beginning farmers)
eligibleActivities: Purchase of agricultural land
Purchase of depreciable machinery or equipment
Purchase of breeding livestock or buildings
Improving existing buildings or farmland
financialCriteria: Net worth of no more than $901,000
Access to adequate working capital, equipment, and other items necessary to operate the farm
No restriction on off-farm income
Cannot be used to refinance existing debt
agriculturalCriteria: Sufficient education, training or experience for the anticipated farm operations
Own no more land than 30% of the county median acres
Be the owner/operator
fundingRange: Land: $682,700. Farm improvements and new depreciable property: $250,000. Used depreciable property: $62,500.
deadline: Applications reviewed monthly; submit to IADD by the first of the month for the monthly board meeting.
requiredDocuments: Beginning Farmer Loan Program Application (completed with lender or seller)
Financial statement
Background letter
Nonrefundable $100 application fee
verificationNotes: Checked the eligibility, loan maximums, fees and process on the official IADD page. iowafinance.com now redirects to opportunityiowa.gov.
fitRationale: The program is for beginning farmers and caps net worth at $901,000. It also limits owned land to 30% of the county median acres. An established 20+ year operation with about 800 owned acres and roughly $1.4M of equipment almost certainly exceeds these limits.

name: Iowa Cover Crop Cost-Share Program (Water Quality Initiative)
agency: Iowa Department of Agriculture and Land Stewardship (IDALS)
description: The Iowa Department of Agriculture and Land Stewardship runs an annual statewide cost-share program for cover crops, open to first-time and returning users in all 99 counties. It also offers per-acre incentives for first-time users who move acres to no-till or strip-till or use a nitrogen inhibitor with fall fertilizer. Applications go through county Soil and Water Conservation District offices.
geography: Iowa (all 99 counties); enhanced Greater Des Moines Watershed incentives in 22 listed counties
eligibleActivities: Planting cover crops
Transitioning acres to no-till or strip-till
Using a nitrogen inhibitor when applying fall fertilizer
financialCriteria: Cost-share limited to 160 acres per participant (statewide program)
Funding is limited
agriculturalCriteria: Cover crops: first-time and returning users eligible at different rates
No-till/strip-till and nitrogen inhibitor incentives listed for first-time users
fundingRange: Farmers planting cover crops for the first time are eligible for $30 per acre. Farmers who have previously planted cover crops are eligible for $20 per acre. Cost-share funding through the statewide program is limited to 160 acres per participant.
deadline: 2026 sign-up opened July 7, 2026; no closing date stated — funding is limited and farmers are encouraged to enroll as soon as possible.
requiredDocuments: Application through the county Soil and Water Conservation District office or costshare.iowaagriculture.gov
verificationNotes: Checked the 2026 rates, the 160-acre cap and how to apply in the official IDALS July 7, 2026 news release. The source is a news release, not a standing program page, and we did not confirm the 2026 closing date. Story County is not one of the 22 counties in the enhanced Greater Des Moines Watershed program announced June 22, 2026.
fitRationale: Smith Family Farms is an Iowa row-crop farm interested in cover crops, and this statewide program is open to farmers in all 99 counties. Cost-share covers at most 160 of the 2,400 acres. Story County is not on the enhanced watershed list.

name: Section 179 Expensing and 100% Additional First-Year (Bonus) Depreciation
agency: Internal Revenue Service (U.S. Department of the Treasury)
description: Under the Working Families Tax Cuts Act (One Big Beautiful Bill Act), businesses can elect to expense up to $2,500,000 of section 179 property in the year it is placed in service. The amount phases down once total section 179 purchases exceed $4,000,000. The law also makes permanent a 100% first-year (bonus) depreciation deduction for qualified property acquired after January 19, 2025.
eligibleEntities: Taxpayers (businesses) placing qualifying section 179 or bonus-depreciation property in service
eligibleActivities: Purchase of equipment and machinery (section 179 / qualified property)
Other depreciable business property placed in service
financialCriteria: Section 179 limit of $2,500,000, reduced dollar-for-dollar when section 179 property placed in service exceeds $4,000,000
Amounts indexed for inflation for tax years beginning after 2025
fundingRange: Increased the total amount a Taxpayer can elect to expense under IRC § 179 from $1,000,000 to $2,500,000 for section 179 property placed in service in tax years beginning after December 31, 2024. The $2,500,000 amount is reduced (but not below zero) by the amount by which the cost of section 179 property placed in service during the taxable year exceeds $4,000,000.
deadline: Claimed for the tax year the property is placed in service (on the annual return).
requiredDocuments: Form 4562, Depreciation and Amortization (per IRS Publication 946)
Records of property cost and placed-in-service date
verificationNotes: Checked the section 179 limits and the permanent 100% bonus depreciation for property acquired after Jan. 19, 2025 on the IRS Working Families Tax Cuts business provisions page. Form 4562 is referenced from Publication 946 and its instructions, which we did not read in full. LLC and member-level rules and income limits were not reviewed, so this needs a tax professional.
fitRationale: A planned ~$250K equipment purchase is well under the section 179 limit, and the IRS page lists equipment and machinery among the purchases the provisions mainly help. The actual tax benefit depends on the LLC's and members' tax situations, and a tax advisor should confirm it.
